quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: You see a green light ahead, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Do not enter until you can drive completely across.
Drive into the intersection and wait for traffic to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter until you can drive completely across.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, never enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way through before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light means you should:

options.text: Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and go when the way is clear.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means "be careful." Slow down, look both ways, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right due to road work.
Slow down because the road curves sharply ahead.
A road crosses from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road curves sharply ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves at a sharp angle ahead. Slow down before you reach the curve, just as you would at a sharp turn.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Vehicles coming toward you going straight or turning right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles coming toward you going straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: When making a left turn, you must yield to all vehicles coming from the opposite direction. This includes cars, bicycles, and motorcycles.

questions.question: Strong wind gusts on highways can:
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers, not just large vehicle drivers. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dust and dirt, and it can also physically move your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A sharp right turn is ahead.
A road joins from the right.
The road ahead curves sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you the road will curve sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to safely cross. You must always stop for pedestrians who are in a crosswalk.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle approaching from the right.
The vehicle approaching from the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle approaching from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection without traffic control signs or signals, you must yield to a vehicle approaching from your right.

questions.question: Which statement best describes defensive driving?

options.text: Assuming other drivers will do the right thing.
Thinking about what other drivers might do and being ready to react.
Expecting no help and giving none to others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Thinking about what other drivers might do and being ready to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means anticipating mistakes from other drivers and being prepared to respond safely.

questions.question: Motorcycles and scooters are hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can hide in your blind spots or be missed easily. Always check carefully for motorcycles and scooters on the road.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Beer affects you less than wine.
Wine affects you less than beer.
Hard ciders and mixed drinks affect you the most.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol harms your reflexes and judgment. The type of drink does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream matters.

questions.question: You have a green light and there are pedestrians in the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: You have the right to go first.

questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross first, even with a green light. Drivers must yield to pedestrians when turning on a green light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the road becomes slippery when it rains.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low railroad crossing. Railroad tracks cross the road at a steep angle. Low vehicles may get stuck or their bottoms may drag on the tracks.

questions.question: Which statement is true about medications and driving?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines are safe for driving if you take the right amount.
Prescription medicines are always safe to drive with.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medicines, prescription or over-the-counter, can be dangerous while driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy and affect your driving. You must know how your medicine affects your ability to drive.

questions.question: What do drivers need to do on interstate highways?

options.text: Be able to drive safely at high speeds.

questions.explanation: Safe highway driving requires you to stay alert and be able to drive safely at high speeds.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road with no bike lane and a bicyclist is ahead of you going the same way. How should you pass safely?

options.text: Slow down, check for oncoming traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
Drive straight. The bicyclist should move out of your way.
Wait until you reach a traffic light or stop sign to pass.
Honk to warn the bicyclist you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, check for oncoming traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: Pass bicyclists like you would pass any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space between your mirror and the bicyclist, or 5 feet on faster roads or with groups. Do not honk unless needed, as it may scare the rider and cause a crash.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other roads and thaw out after other roads. This happens because cold air blows under bridges from both sides.

questions.question: What should you do if you see an animal on the road?
questions.explanation: Always be careful when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid scaring it.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to create more distance.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to spot tailgaters or fast-approaching cars. If someone is following too close, slow down and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if you don't see any traffic.
Signal only if there is traffic nearby.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy night traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if you don't see any traffic.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb. Do not skip signaling—it is the law and keeps you safe.

questions.question: A flashing red light means:

options.text: The same as a stop sign.
You do not have to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: Using which of these increases crash risk for distracted drivers?
questions.explanation: Cell phones, radios, and CD players all distract drivers. Using any of these while driving increases crash risk.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road is slippery when wet. Drive slowly and carefully.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a yellow light and have not entered yet. You should:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Slow down and go through carefully.

questions.explanation: When you see a yellow light, prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, clear it quickly. If you have not entered, stop safely.

questions.question: As a vehicle's speed increases, stopping distance and collision severity:
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and worse crashes. As you go faster, increase your following distance to give yourself time to stop safely.

questions.question: A bicyclist who breaks traffic laws:

options.text: Does not have to obey traffic laws.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and duties as drivers. They must follow traffic laws and can be ticketed if they break them.

questions.question: At a light rail crossing, always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Look both ways, obey all signals, and remember that trains share the road with cars and bicycles.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic driving straight. Turn only when you can safely do so without affecting oncoming cars.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking, reduces alertness, and affects your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: A traffic light changes from green to yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross before the red light.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before reaching the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before reaching the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. You should be ready to stop before the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You must come to a complete stop at an intersection when you see a:
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, look both ways, and only cross when it is safe.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Keep driving at your normal speed.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be alert. Proceed with caution through the intersection.

questions.question: When is it legal to drive faster than the posted speed limit?

options.text: When there is no other traffic in your lane.
When you are passing another vehicle.

questions.explanation: It is always illegal to drive faster than the speed limit, even when passing another vehicle.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from certain lanes. A green arrow means:

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
You may go, and you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may only proceed if the green arrow appears with a green circle light.
It shows the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go, and you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. You must turn in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: If you are stopped and a police officer suspects you have been drinking, you:

options.text: Cannot refuse to take a breath test.
Can refuse the test if you have not been drinking.
Can refuse the test if you think you will fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot refuse to take a breath test.
questions.explanation: Wisconsin law requires you to take a breath test if a police officer asks. You cannot refuse.

questions.question: Which types of drugs can affect your ability to drive?
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medications. Driving while impaired by any drug is against the law.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign mean?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.
Construction work is happening or ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is happening or ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn about construction, maintenance, or emergency work.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line between two lanes mean?

options.text: Both lanes of traffic move in the same direction.
You can pass when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line separates lanes moving in opposite directions. You can pass when there is no oncoming traffic in the passing lane.

questions.question: When driving closely behind another vehicle at night, use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when you are within 500 feet of another vehicle or in heavy traffic.

questions.question: When is it safe to move back into the right lane after passing a vehicle on the left?

options.text: When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can move back into the right lane when you see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which action blocks the smooth flow of traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes causes traffic to back up. You should avoid this behavior.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Lanes are moving in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Lanes are moving in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Lanes are moving in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Lanes are moving in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes are moving in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle does not have anti-lock brakes, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes helps you stop quickly while keeping control of the steering.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: The blind spots around trucks and buses.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around trucks and buses.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on the sides, rear, and front. Your vehicle cannot be seen in these areas. These are called the "No zone."

questions.question: When should you not enter an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red?

options.text: Unless you entered the intersection on a yellow light.
Unless you entered the intersection on a green light.

questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can cross completely before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: What effect does excessive speed have?

options.text: It does not increase crash risk.
It often leads to poor decision-making.

questions.correctAnswerText: It often leads to poor decision-making.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed causes many crashes. It does not save time and often leads to poor decision-making.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that left turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic signal has the same requirements as:
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing red signal, you must stop and let all other traffic pass.
